SECOND REVIEW PASS, 2026-10-02. One OMD2 mesh can become TWO OMD3 meshes: OMD2 models a banner and its pole as one mesh, OMD3 ships them separately, so `members` (a list placed together) joins `member` (one choice) and `family` (pick by size).

A sibling proposal is NOT safe when the name carries a modifier: `Wall1_2Angled` proposed the `Wall_FB` family from `Wall1_2` and the right answer is `WallAngled_1_2` exactly; `WallCandle01` proposed a wall family and is a decoration. A modifier word (Angled, Candle) names a different family, so it must beat the stem match.

Six entries are deliberately UNRESOLVED rather than guessed: archedwall, ThicknessCorner, OD_DebriProp (nothing offered fits) and MiniStep1A/2b (no 1:1 stairs). MEASURED FROM SHIPPED LEVELS, 2026-10-02 (9 levels, 23,182 pieces). Archways: of the 17 Archway* meshes in the catalogue the shipped levels place only TWO -- Archway_1x1x3_Short_RB (288) and Archway_1x1x4_Short_RB (225). What surrounds them is the pattern the reviewer meant: ColumnTrim_CastStone_150W (387 within 700uu), Metal_Trim_Join_Small_Rivet (279), Column_Sec_1_4_RB (166), Metal_PostBase_B (161), Torch (156), ColumnTrim_CastStone_900W (143). So an OMD3 archway is an arch piece plus side columns plus metal trim, and archways also stack 600uu above each other.

STAIR SLOPE AGREES BETWEEN THE GAMES. OMD2 stairs rise 600uu over ~1200uu of depth (26.5 degrees) and OMD3 Stairs_*_4_SB rise 606 over 1211 -- the same. So stairs convert without reshaping, and 3widestairs -> Stairs_4x_4_SB is 1200 wide on both sides at scale 1.0. OMD3 naming is Stairs_<width in cells>x_<rise>_SB, where _05_ is a shallow single step and a missing rise is the default.

PROVISIONAL entries carry confidence "provisional" and were never seen by the reviewer. They exist so emission can be exercised; silence on a review sheet is NOT agreement -- the reviewer rejected 2 of the 19 proposals outright, so the rate is about 1 in 10.
